prompt: A 74-year-old man with heart failure takes furosemide daily and is admitted after several days of vomiting and poor oral intake. His creatinine has increased from 1.0 to 2.0 mg/dL. At the time of urine collection, blood urea nitrogen is 40 mg/dL, urine urea nitrogen is 300 mg/dL, and urine creatinine is 60 mg/dL. Because recent loop-diuretic exposure can confound the fractional excretion of sodium, calculate the fractional excretion of urea (FEUrea) and interpret the result using a 35% cutoff.

rubric_items.text: States the FEUrea formula as (urine urea nitrogen × plasma creatinine) / (blood urea nitrogen × urine creatinine) × 100, or shows an equivalent calculation.
States the FEUrea as 25%; exact value required, with a tolerance of ±0.1 percentage point.
States that an FEUrea below 35% supports a prerenal/hemodynamic cause of the acute kidney injury in this clinical context.
Explains that FEUrea is being used because loop-diuretic exposure may increase urine sodium and make FENa less reliable.
